title: Sonny and the Kookaburra Chick | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka hears a soft practising sound from high in a gum tree and discovers a young kookaburra chick quietly rehearsing its laugh all by itself in the moonlight. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
There was a sound coming from the gum tree.

Not the full kookaburra laugh — not the loud, rollicking, all-the-bush-can-hear sound. This was quieter. Softer. A little uncertain.

Sunny stopped and looked up.

High in the branches she could see a shape — a young kookaburra, sitting alone on a branch in the moonlight. Brown and fluffy and a little too big for its branch, which bent slightly under its weight.

It was practising.

She could hear it now — the hesitant beginning of a laugh, stopping partway through, then starting again from the beginning. A small attempt. A pause. Another attempt, a bit louder. Another pause.

It didn't have it yet. The laugh came out a little wobbly in the middle. But it kept trying.

Sunny smiled.

She sat down at the base of the tree and listened.

The chick tried again. This time a little better — the opening cackle came out right, the middle wobbled only a little, and the ending was almost there.

It paused.

Then it tried once more.

Better. Definitely better.

She thought: everything worth learning sounds a little wobbly at first.

The chick was quiet for a long moment. Then it made one more soft attempt, and this one had something in it — something more certain — before it stopped and tucked its beak under its wing.

Goodnight, little practiser.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, kookaburra chick. Goodnight, little one.
